title: The Cambridge History of Early Modern English Literature
reliability_notes: The standard collaborative history of English literature 1500–1700; used as the primary framework for period coverage, movements, and canonical selection in Installment 3.

title: English Literature in the Sixteenth Century, Excluding Drama
publisher: Oxford University Press (The Oxford History of English Literature, vol. 3)
reliability_notes: The classic single-author survey of sixteenth-century English literature; used for canonical judgements, periodization, and the assessment of the 'drab' and 'golden' styles.

title: The Oxford Handbook of Tudor Literature, 1485–1603
reliability_notes: Authoritative essay collection on Tudor literature in its material and political contexts; used for biographical and bibliographical verification of the early Tudor authors.

title: The Norton Anthology of English Literature, 10th edition, Volume B: The Sixteenth Century and the Early Seventeenth Century
reliability_notes: Standard classroom anthology; used for establishing the canonical core of the period and for texts in modern spelling.

title: Sir Thomas Wyatt: The Complete Poems
reliability_notes: The standard modern edition of Wyatt's verse; used for titles, dates, and textual facts of the Wyatt canon.

title: The Book of Common Prayer: The Texts of 1549, 1559, and 1662
reliability_notes: Standard modern edition of the Prayer Book texts; used for the liturgical record of the Reformation settlement.

title: Tudor Drama before Shakespeare, 1485–1590: New Directions for Research, Criticism, and Pedagogy
author_or_editor: Lloyd Edward Kermode, Jason Scott-Warren, and Martine van Elk (eds.)
reliability_notes: Scholarly survey of early Tudor drama; used for dates and contexts of the interludes and moralities.

title: The King's Reformation: Henry VIII and the Remaking of the English Church
reliability_notes: Standard modern history of the Henrician Reformation; used for the political and ecclesiastical context of the polemical literature.

title: Poetry and Politics in the English Renaissance, revised edition
reliability_notes: Influential study of the political dimension of Renaissance poetry; used for the political reading of Skelton, Wyatt, and Surrey.
